articles.title: Misery Index: Arch Manning, Steve Sarkisian and Texas don't seem to have answers and are running out of time
articles.summary: With all the parity these days, it's hard to tell the real problems from the temporary circumstances. But the things plaguing Texas right now are not new.
articles.body:
As we walk through this new world of college football together, it's going to be more and more difficult to distinguish between the results we can chalk up to parity and those that are worth freaking out about.

It's true, the differences between elite teams and the middle class are smaller than ever. The schedules, particularly in the SEC this year, are unforgiving. A team's overall health matters. Fatigue, both physical and emotional, is hard to measure until you see it on the field. Nearly anyone can beat anyone on a given day. Like the NFL, margins are brutally small.

Things are so different now in college football that it's tempting to show a little more patience and understanding.

Of course, that's not what we do here at the Misery Index. We are about finding the pain that fans experience and telling them why it's real and deserved. And the best way to do that is to look past the roller coaster of results we see on a week-in, week-out basis and focus on the things that fit within established patterns.

Which is really, really bad news for Texas and coach Steve Sarkisian.

Because if you look at what's become of Texas this season, it's hard to make a case that back-to-back losses to Oklahoma and Florida are the product of bad luck or an emotional hangover or exhaustion caused by too many physical games.

You can find a good explanation for plenty of the surprising results in the SEC this season. But losing to an inferior Oklahoma team coming off a bye week ? Then turning around at home and blowing a 17-3 lead over Florida, only to lose 27-24 ?

Not only are there zero excuses for a Texas team that has tumbled from No. 1 to fighting for its College Football Playoff life, it isn't even that surprising if you watch the Longhorns every week.

They are always less than the sum of their parts.

You know it, Texas fans know it and deep down Texas athletic director Chris Del Conte must know it: As long as Sarkisian is your head coach, you will always leave some food on the table.

That doesn't mean Sarkisian is incompetent or that Texas would be better off with someone else. We've seen what bad Texas looks like, and Sarkisian has left those days in the rear-view mirror. He's 39-10 over the last 3 1/2 seasons with a couple appearances in the CFP.

But how many times over his 13 years as a head coach have we ended a season saying that Sarkisian got the most out of his talent or exceeded expectations? Once, maybe? And yet how often do we have to rationalize why someone who made his reputation as an elite play-caller isn't putting an elite offense on the field?

This Texas team was one of the most expensive rosters and built to win it all. It got a massive Week 2 win over Ohio State . Its quarterback, Arch Manning, is still projected to be a first-round NFL Draft pick . And yet, if Texas got left out of the CFP for a second year in a row, there would be zero room to complain after Saturday. That's how much of a reputation hit Texas has taken by losing to an Oklahoma team that couldn't score and a Florida team that hasn't stopped anyone all season. Texas, in fact, is the only power conference team that hasn't managed to crack 30 points against a Gators defense that ranked 131st in pass defense.

Yes, Manning is flawed, and maybe that makes it hard to do all the things Sarkisian wants to do. But the macro issue is largely the same as it was when Quinn Ewers was the quarterback: It's harder for Texas to score points than it should be, which points directly to Sarkisian because he calls the plays. And Texas' overall inconsistency, where it will just kick away one game per season that it can't afford to lose, is a Sark staple going back to his time at USC and Washington before that.

With all the parity these days, it's hard to tell the real problems from the temporary circumstances. But the things plaguing Texas right now are not new, making them America's most miserable fan base in Week 7.

ACC: The misery felt by Virginia fans should not just be about slipping to 4-3 this season after a 23-13 loss to SMU. Much of it, if not the bulk of it, should really extend back to last year's ACC championship game when the Cavaliers blew it against Duke. Why does that game seem so relevant now? Because when you're Virginia, you're probably not going to get many cracks at making the playoff. Between 2005 and 2024, Virginia finished a season in the top 25 just one time — and that was 2019 when the final coaches' poll ranked them … 25th. So when you have a chance to do something historic for your program, you can't let it slip by against a Duke team that somehow got into the ACC title game at 7-5. If Virginia won that game, it would have been a playoff team. You can hang banners for that these days. Tony Elliott would have been just the second coach in program history to win a conference title. Despite some high hopes for what this season could be, former Missouri/Penn State quarterback Beau Pribula hasn't worked out and Virginia is back to the middle of the pack. It's hard to keep the faith that Virginia is going to have such a golden opportunity any time in the foreseeable future.

Big Ten: We're going to make this very simple for Matt Campbell. At Toledo and Iowa State, you can recruit a bunch of guys with three-star talent but five-star hearts, win seven or eight games because you've got a really good culture and get a pat on the head at the end of the season. That's not going to cut it at Penn State. Even the most pessimistic projections of Campbell's first season were not as bad as the reality of being 0-4 in the Big Ten after a 21-18 loss at Michigan. And even if somehow Penn State crushes the soft back end of its schedule to finish 8-4 (which is certainly no guarantee given what we've seen so far), it will mean absolutely nothing other than a scorching hot seat for both Campbell and athletic director Pat Kraft heading into Year 2. Even if you were on board with Penn State firing James Franklin last year amidst a three-game losing streak, nobody signed up for going directly to the bottom of the Big Ten.

Big 12: The last time Kansas beat Kansas State in football, one of the players in the losing locker room was a freshman quarterback in the middle of a redshirt year named Collin Klein. That was 2008. The next season, Kansas State got revenge 17-10 in Manhattan. Now, fast-forward to 2026 and Klein is the first-year head coach at his alma mater. In other words, during his nearly two decades as part of the Kansas State program from player to assistant to head coach, Klein's only loss to Kansas was his first year as a college student. That's how brutal this rivalry has been on the Jayhawks, who fell to 2-4 after a 35-24 loss. Even though Kansas has had some good moments under Lance Leipold (though fewer of them lately, as he's lost 14 of his last 21 in the Big 12), the Sunflower Showdown has trended toward bug-meets-windshield territory. And among those 18 consecutive losses, only four have been decided by one score.

Group of Six: If you're trying to find this year's hard-luck team, look no further than Navy. Leading UTSA 34-31 inside the final five minutes, two Midshipmen missed a tackle on A'Marion Peterson, who turned a screen pass into a 41-yard touchdown and ultimately a 38-34 win. Since beating Towson on Sept. 5, Navy has lost four one-score games — by eight to FAU, by four to UAB, by five to Air Force and by four to UTSA. What made Saturday's result even more painful was that Navy quarterback Jackson Gutierrez didn't get a celebrate a win in his hometown despite rushing for 139 yards and two touchdowns and throwing for two more. After going 21-5 the last two years, this is a surprising step back for Navy, which was picked to win the American this year by most of the preseason publications.

Marcus Freeman: No matter how good of a team we think Notre Dame is, we need to keep one important fact in mind. The Irish, quite simply, have not beaten a team that matters since the College Football Playoff semifinals on Jan. 9, 2025. That's not an indictment of Freeman's ability to win big games, which we have seen plenty of times in the past. It is, however, an indictment of Notre Dame's scheduling philosophy of late. Sorry, but when you are watching college football week after week and how tough it is to survive week to week in the Big Ten, SEC or even the Big 12 in some cases, Notre Dame is doing itself no favors in terms of public perception by playing good teams so infrequently. No, a 28-24 loss to BYU in Provo should not be disqualifying. But if schedules matter, and they're supposed to in this ultra-subjective playoff system, you can't reward Notre Dame for scheduling two big games a year if they aren't winning them. Going 0-2 last season against Miami and Texas A&M cost them a CFP bid. If the Irish don't beat Miami on Nov. 7, they won't have anything close to a high-quality win this year and shouldn't be in the CFP.

Clark Lea: OK, so maybe Vanderbilt's success was (mostly) due to Diego Pavia after all. That is the only possible takeaway from watching the post-Pavia Commodores, who are back to being the worst team in the SEC after a 31-21 home loss to Arkansas. With what's left of their schedule, Vandy desperately needed this one to have hopes of making a bowl game. Instead, the Commodores' defense gave up 438 yards and freshman quarterback Jared Curtis threw two interceptions. Lea secured a big contract extension after going 10-3 last season. But without Pavia, his record is 12-30. Yes, Vanderbilt is a tough job — arguably one of the toughest in the power conferences. But last year's narrative was all about Vandy turning a corner and committing more resources to football, which included a massive NIL deal for Curtis to renege on his commitment to Georgia. It's concerning that things have immediately returned to the historical norm in Nashville.

Mike Norvell: The last two plays of Florida State's 43-35 overtime loss to Miami will haunt Norvell for awhile. Not because of anything he or his players did but because when things aren't going well generally in a football program, it seems even the good plays get punished. Such was the case in the second overtime, as Florida State quarterback Ashton Daniels threw two Hail Marys — neither of which hit the ground — and yet saw both wiped out by rulings that Norvell will find hard to swallow. The first one, which Daniels completed from the 36-yard line, got wiped out by a fairly ticky-tack holding penalty. Backed up to the 46, Daniels again gave his receiver a great shot to catch the ball. Instead, it was ruled an interception as the Miami defender and Florida State receiver came down with it almost simultaneously. On replay, it was almost impossible to tell. But because the call on the field was an interception rather than simultaneous possession, which would have been a touchdown, the initial call withstood the review. Playing so competitively against the Canes may have bought Norvell more time, but a 3-4 record is still a 3-4 record.

Pat Fitzgerald: Though it's unclear how much money he got out of Northwestern in order to settle his wrongful-termination lawsuit, it was almost certainly in the tens of millions. And it probably wasn't enough to completely soothe the pain he felt losing 24-21 to his alma mater, as Northwestern's Jackson Kleather nailed a 34-yard field goal to beat Michigan State on the final play from scrimmage. For those who don't remember, Fitzgerald was a star linebacker on Northwestern's miraculous 1995 team that made the Rose Bowl, took over as head coach in 2006 following the tragic death of Randy Walker and led the program for 17 seasons, some of which were very good. But it all fell apart in the summer of 2023, several months after a 1-11 season, when allegations surfaced about a culture of locker room hazing. Fitzgerald denied any knowledge of it but was fired anyway. It was an ugly and personally hurtful end to a great relationship, and Fitzgerald's motivation for coming back at another Big Ten school almost certainly revolves around revenge on some level. How could it not? But that will have to wait at least another year.

Gunner gacked one: If there's one quarterback you wouldn't expect to commit a horrible turnover at the worst possible time, it's probably Georgia's Gunner Stockton. With his maturity and experience in big games, it was absolutely stunning to see him cough up a fumble just past midfield with a minute to go against Auburn, setting the table for a 27-24 loss. At that point in the game, Georgia had just come back to tie it up and forced Auburn to punt. Despite how poorly Georgia played for much of the game, nearly everyone watching is probably thinking the same thing — that Stockton is about to lead his team into field goal range and Georgia will walk off the field 7-0. Instead, Stockton's turnover handed Auburn the opportunity to pull one of the upsets of the year and the Tigers did not give it back.

Mora defense, please: When we last saw Colorado State a couple weeks ago, head coach Jim Mora was having a meltdown about how bad the Rams' defense was, leading him to fire coordinator Tyson Summers mid-game. Shockingly (or not), that didn't solve Colorado State's problems on that side of the ball. In a 66-27 loss to Texas State, the Rams gave up 716 yards of offense, including 503 on the ground. It's probably worth asking in retrospect why Mora hired Summers in the first place. They had never worked together before, and Summers' defensive scheme has nothing in common with what Mora's teams had done in the past. But Summers, who was Colorado State's interim coach last season, was well-liked enough that Mora kept him around. As a result, this is pretty much a wasted year for the Rams, who have given up 222 total points in their last four games.

Mateer isn't magic: Oklahoma is just painful to watch on offense at this point. Sure, it doesn't help that the offensive line is banged up and isn't playing very well. But the question Sooners fans will be asking for a long time to come is what the heck happened to quarterback John Mateer. Though Mateer has always had flaws, at least he was fun to watch last season. But this year has gone so poorly, it's making Oklahoma fans pine for the days of Blake Bell. Though the Belldozer was not an elite quarterback by any means — he ultimately found his calling as a tight end — he didn't make the crushing mistakes week after week that we're seeing from Mateer. In a 21-13 loss to Kentucky, which all but eliminates OU from the playoff conversation, Mateer threw three interceptions. Two of them came on Oklahoma's final two possessions, including a pick-6 when the Sooners merely needed a field goal to escape with a victory. Taking special teams and defensive scores out of the equation, Oklahoma's offense hasn't produced more than 14 points in any game besides the season opener against UTEP.

Fans gone wild: One week after an Alabama fan struck a Georgia player on the helmet during the postgame celebration, earning him a lifetime ban from attending games in Tuscaloosa, video surfaced of a Texas fan on the field taunting Florida players after the Gators' 27-24 win in Austin. While the fan had the middle finger of his right hand raised, he was holding a cell phone in his left, suggesting he wanted this incident on camera and distributed on social media. Quite simply, this needs to stop. While it's indicative of a much larger societal problem — young people seem to have fewer and fewer inhibitions about bringing bad online behavior into real-life scenarios — this is also something schools need to get control over. Between all the premium access being sold and sideline passes handed out, it just seems like there are more and more people finding their way to the field who simply don't belong there. Security at football games is hard and unwieldy, but maybe it's time to tighten things up and start issuing stricter bans for fans who directly engage players with malicious intent — even if it's just trash talk. Figure this out before a truly regrettable and preventable incident happens

articles.title: Premier League hits and misses: Bryan Mbeumo is Manchester United's only reliable goalscorer as Eberechi Eze struggles for Arsenal
articles.summary: Sky Sports' football writers analyse Sunday's Premier League action; Bryan Mbeumo continues to offer glimmer of hope for Man Utd; Eberechi Eze needs to show his worth to Arsenal with others in wait; Nottingham Forest's lack of goals continue to concern
articles.body:
Michael Carrick called Manchester United's 1-1 draw with Leeds a "fresh start" on Sunday. No doubt that encapsulated the sense of relief the manager felt after watching his side battle and duel better than they had all season, showing the commitment that had been missing from most performances so far.

He will be pleased Bryan Mbeumo's form is a continuation of what went before, though - about the only player who has shown a shade of consistency during this difficult start. Three of Mbeumo's four Premier League goals have put United 1-0 ahead this term.

His strike against Leeds marked an important momentum shift in a game that could have otherwise got away from them. Fortunately for Carrick, Mbeumo has been a reliant source since his switch from Brentford, his 15 goals more than any other United player since his debut - including Bruno Fernandes.

Just two victories from 10 games in all competitions means Carrick is not off the hook. But while Mbeumo keeps scoring, he's got something positive to hook performances on. Especially while Fernandes continues to look off-colour. Laura Hunter

Eberechi Eze has spent a year at Arsenal since leaving Crystal Palace, but questions remain over whether he is ready to become one of the club's leading figures as their ambitions continue to grow.

His talent is undeniable. The real concern is whether he can influence games consistently, and the trip to Nottingham Forest presented another opportunity to silence his doubters.

With Arsenal struggling to break down Forest, Eze had the chance to make a difference. Instead, he was substituted at half-time, watching from the sidelines as Noni Madueke replaced him and went on to score the 80th-minute winner.

Roy Keane's assessment on Sky Sports was telling, suggesting his concerns extended beyond a single performance.

"We're still waiting for him, the talent is there," Keane said. "We just want him to be at Arsenal and be able to take responsibility and try to be the main man at a big club."

That is the challenge facing Eze. At Crystal Palace, he was the focal point, the player expected to create chances and turn games in his team's favour. At Arsenal, however, talent alone will not earn him that status. He must deliver consistently, particularly in tight contests when his team need inspiration.

Ian Wright offered some important context, describing Eze as a "moments player" who benefits from having players around him and can become isolated on the left.

There is merit to that argument. Eze offers a different threat to Madueke, whose pace, directness and willingness to take on defenders gave Arsenal a fresh dimension in the second half.

Yet that only underlines the challenge facing the former Palace man. While Madueke seized his opportunity and made an immediate impact, Eze failed to leave his mark on the contest.

Competition for places is healthy at a club with Arsenal's ambitions. For Eze, though, the task is no longer simply to showcase his ability in flashes. He must demonstrate that he can influence games regularly, take responsibility when his team need him and establish himself as a first-choice player.

The talent is there. Now, Eze must prove he can turn that potential into consistent performances and become one of Arsenal's main men. William Bitibiri

There was only so long Nottingham Forest could rely on defensive resilience before their lack of goals caught up with them. Now they are in the relegation zone.

Oliver Glasner's side have failed to score in every Premier League home game this season, and their defeat to Arsenal highlighted why they are in trouble.

Forest competed and created opportunities but lacked the quality in the final third to make their efforts count.

Liam Delap struggled to make an impact against Arsenal's defence, summing up a frustrating afternoon. Forest needed someone to take responsibility but their attacking play lacked conviction.

That is the worry for Glasner. Defensive organisation can only take a team so far; they still need goals to win matches.

Forest are now in the relegation zone with just five points. Their performances offer some encouragement, but until they find a reliable source of goals at the City Ground, it is difficult to see their situation improving. William Bitibiri

There was a time when Hurzeler could barely win over his own supporters. Now he has Brighton dreaming again.

Back in February, Hurzeler was booed off at the Amex after a 1-0 home defeat to Crystal Palace. The frustration was palpable. Questions were being asked, patience was wearing thin.

Fast forward to this 5-0 demolition of their fiercest rivals and the transformation is remarkable.

This is what happens when a club refuses to panic. Brighton could have pulled the trigger when the noise around Hurzeler was at its loudest. Instead, they trusted their process and back their man.

Brighton have always prided themselves on smart decision-making, from recruitment to managerial appointments.

Hurzeler is the latest example of that philosophy working.

And what better way to underline that progress than by dismantling Palace?

The boos of February feel a long way away. Brighton are going places. Lewis Jones

Crystal Palace won three trophies in the previous two seasons. On this evidence, they look a million miles away from those glories.

This was Pierre Sage's worst day as Palace boss by some distance. There have been defeats this season where you could at least point to some decent football, a positive spell or an individual performance worth celebrating. At the Amex, there was nothing. No resistance, no response.

Brighton ripped them apart in a 5-0 humiliation that exposed just how far Palace have fallen. The defensive holes were glaring. Replacing Marc Guehi and Maxence Lacroix was never going to be straightforward but the scale of the problem is becoming impossible to ignore. Palace look vulnerable every time opponents turn up the pressure.

Last weekend, Nottingham Forest missed seven big chances in their defeat to Palace. That was a warning sign, perhaps one that was easy to dismiss with three points in the bag. Brighton offered no such charity. They punished Palace's mistakes ruthlessly.

Sage must find answers quickly. If Palace continue to concede chances at this rate, the pressure on their manager will grow with every passing week. Their recent trophy haul feels a long way away. Lewis Jones

Bournemouth head coach Marco Rose must have grown tired of constantly explaining how well his side had played in defeat this season, a recurring theme for the Cherries as they looked for a first Premier League win of the season under their new head coach, but no more after Sunday's much-needed, but hugely deserved victory over fellow strugglers Sunderland.

Sure, the hosts were helped on their way to the the three points by some calamitous defending from the Black Cats, but it was more that they forced their opponents into those mistakes, including for both their goals, as well as Kevin Danso's 17th-minute red card.

In fact, such was Bournemouth's dominance from start to finish at the Vitality that their final xG of 4.46 was their highest on record in the Premier League, with the German even joking after the game that he might now treat himself to a non-alcoholic beer.

It may have taken Bournemouth seven league matches to get off the mark but anyone who has watched them this season knows that first victory was just around the corner. They must now build on it, especially at home, where they have lost one of their last 15 top-flight contests.

Maintaining the Vitality as a fortress will go a long way to ensuring another fine campaign. Rich Morgan

articles.title: Lamine llega desatado a 'su' semana grande
articles.standfirst: El catalán, además, se crece ante los escenarios de renombre
articles.summary: El catalán, además, se crece ante los escenarios de renombre
articles.body: Si Lamine Yamal ya estaba llamado a ser uno de los grandes protagonistas de la próxima semana en el Barcelona, sus últimas actuaciones en la segunda parte del duelo contra el Galatasaray y el cruce en La Cartuja no han hecho más que multiplicar las expectativas. El joven extremo llega a uno de los tramos más exigentes de la temporada, con PSG y Real Madrid, en un estado de forma extraordinario, firmando jugadas, regates y disparos que parecen sacados de un videojuego y trasladados directamente al terreno de juego. Además, el futbolista de Rocafonda nunca ha escondido que los grandes escenarios representan una motivación especial para él. Y si hay dos rivales capaces de despertar al máximo su competitividad, esos son el PSG y el Real Madrid. El Barcelona afronta una de las semanas más importantes de la temporada. No tanto por el carácter definitivo de los resultados, ya que todavía queda mucho camino por recorrer tanto en la Champions como en LaLiga, sino por la dimensión de los desafíos que tiene por delante. El conjunto azulgrana se medirá este martes al PSG en un encuentro que servirá para medir sus aspiraciones europeas frente a uno de los grandes candidatos al título. El domingo, además, llegará el Clásico, una oportunidad para dar un golpe sobre la mesa en el campeonato regular. Dos partidos de máxima exigencia en los que la inspiración de Lamine Yamal puede resultar determinante. Y el extremo llega especialmente motivado. A pesar de haber acumulado un importante número de minutos durante el parón de selecciones, Hansi Flick ha seguido contando con él en los compromisos del Barcelona. El desgaste físico podía generar dudas, pero sus últimas actuaciones han demostrado que continúa siendo un futbolista crucial y que no necesita descansar ni rotar. Contra el Galatasaray, en la segunda parte, Lamine se convirtió en el gran protagonista del encuentro. Firmó dos asistencias y participó en la jugada del cuarto tanto azulgrana. Más allá de sus estadísticas, una de las acciones que acaparó buena parte de la atención fue un regate de enorme dificultad técnica que rápidamente dio la vuelta al mundo. Si contra el conjunto turco ya había dejado muestras de su calidad excepcional, el sábado, contra el Betis, volvió a ofrecer un recital. Su gol en el minuto 10 fue una auténtica exhibición: un disparo con la zurda desde la frontal del área, con una rosca exquisita marca de la casa. Pero su actuación no se limitó al gol. Lamine también asistió a Gabriel Jesus y protagonizó varias acciones individuales en las que volvió a exhibir su repertorio. A sus condiciones técnicas se suma, además, una personalidad competitiva que crece cuanto mayor es el desafío. Lamine Yamal disfruta de los partidos de máxima exigencia y no rehúye la responsabilidad cuando el foco se concentra sobre él. Por todo ello, el futbolista de Rocafonda afronta la semana con la moral por las nubes y en un momento especialmente ilusionante. El PSG y el Real Madrid representan dos pruebas de máximo nivel para comprobar hasta dónde puede llegar este Barcelona. Lamine llega lanzado, con confianza, argumentos futbolísticos y ganas de seguir demostrando su candidatura firme al Balón de Oro.

articles.title: El Granada se pone en órbita y deja tocado a Celades
articles.standfirst: Los rojiblancos supieron madurar el partido para tumbar al Cádiz y llevarse los tres puntos
articles.summary: Los rojiblancos supieron madurar el partido para tumbar al Cádiz y llevarse los tres puntos
articles.body: El derbi andaluz entre Granada y Cádiz, con colorido y un gran ambiente en la grada, fue gris y plomizo sobre el terreno de juego, un duelo de digestión lenta que se decantó del lado local gracias a la mayor pegada de los rojiblancos, que exprimieron al máximo sus oportunidades para sumar su tercer triunfo consecutivo y mandar a los gaditanos a la lona. Para arrancar, y evitar sorpresas desagradables en los primeros compases del choque, el Granada asumió una actitud contemplativa, cediéndole la iniciativa al Cádiz mientras los de Pacheta aguardaban pacientes su oportunidad. Tras coger ritmo, fueron los nazaríes lo que tomaron las riendas del juego, mostrándose mucho más propositivos con el balón, aunque con una circulación demasiado previsible, con la que eran incapaces de romper la resistencia del muro amarillo a pesar de intentarlo con disparos de larga distancia de Pascual y Alemañ. Tras un largo pasaje con equilibrio sobre el terreno de juego, sin jugadas de peligro que rompiesen la monotonía, el Cádiz se estiró con dos chispazos aislados que pusieron en alerta a los locales y agitaron el choque en el tramo final del primer acto, con escaramuzas en ambas áreas y un bombardeo de centros por parte del bando rojiblanco, que trataba de llegar al gol por medio de la erosión, una fórmula que tampoco sirvió para romper la igualdad con la que se llegó al descanso. La segunda parte parecía seguir los pasos de los primeros cuarenta y cinco minutos, pero Rodelas decidió cambiar el guión, superando a su marcador para lanzar un centro al corazón del área que terminó encontrando a Gumbau, quien, emulando a Kroos, firmó un pase a la red para subir el 1-0 al marcador y poner de cara el partido para los locales. El tanto sacudió el partido, con el Granada tratando de encontrar la sentencia y el Cádiz buscando el empate, lo que rompió el rigor táctico y todo se desató; un escenario en el que fueron los nazaríes quienes lograron su recompensa con el 2-0, obra de Pascual, que tuvo la frialdad suficiente para parar un segundo dentro del área y ajustar su disparo al palo, imposible para Iván Gil. Con el partido visto para sentencia, los minutos finales fueron un trámite que certificaba el tercer triunfo consecutivo de los rojiblancos, que se acercan al pelotón de cabeza.

articles.title: Javi Rodríguez devuelve la sonrisa al Celta
articles.standfirst: Golazo y asistencia del central ante un Alavés que vendió cara su derrota
articles.summary: Golazo y asistencia del central ante un Alavés que vendió cara su derrota
articles.body: El Celta vuelve a sonreír. La derrota europea ante la Juventus fue un duro palo, pero no tocaba otra que levantarse y espabilar en una Liga en la que, hasta ahora, sólo había ganado un partido. El Alavés dio muestras de que podía prolongar el bajón celeste, pero Javi Rodríguez se encargó de disiparlas. El defensor celebró a lo grande su reciente renovación hasta 2030 con un partido completo y, sobre todo, dos chispazos decisivos cuando más lo necesitaba su equipo. Primero, con un milimétrico pase a Jutglà y, después, con una acción personal más propia de un extremo regateador que de un central. No fue un partido entretenido, sobre todo en la primera mitad. Hubo faltas, balones divididos y pocos metros limpios, en un partido que Munuera Montero tuvo que interrumpir con frecuencia. La primera noticia fue una cartulina al cuarto de hora. Eso explica el poco ritmo con el que comenzó el encuentro. Y es raro en choques donde el Celta está presente. Los locales fueron los primeros en acercarse a la portería de Sivera, aunque sin puntería. Jutglà mandó fuera un disparo en el 26' que debió ajustar mejor, y dos minutos después, Hugo Álvarez buscó la portería por su cuenta, pero su remate se marchó desviado. El Alavés, que tuvo más el balón y se estiró con intención, fue a por su momento en el 30'. Toni Martínez se plantó dentro del área y disparó, pero se encontró con Radu, que respondió bien y evitó el primer gol del partido. Sin embargo, la mejor ocasión fue de Boyé poco después, en un remate de cabeza franco desde el área pequeña que acabó tímidamente en las manos de del meta rumano del Celta. Las cosas cambiaron en la segunda parte cuando Jutglà encontró la red tras un milimétrico pase al hueco de Javi Rodríguez que definió el 9 de primeras. Antes ya había movido fichas Giráldez con la entrada de Febas y Rueda por Moriba y Swedberg, lo que le dio algo más de movilidad al balón en la sala de máquinas. Con más fútbol en la medular y el marcador a favor, el Celta produjo más llegadas. Quique lo vio desde la banda y también agitó el banquillo con un triple cambio en busca de reestablecer el control que había tenido en la primera mitad. Lo que realmente le dio vida al Alavés fue que el Celta no concretase sus ocasiones. Y eso, mantuvo el partido vivo hasta que apareció de nuevo Javi Rodríguez. El defensor céltico completó su gran actuación con un eslalon en el que sorteó hasta cuatro rivales para acabar cruzando el esférico a Sivera en un espacio muy reducido. Un gol que casi dinamitó la moral del Alavés aunque quedaran más de 20 minutos de encuentro. Sin embargo, Novoa se encargó de darle motivos para luchar hasta el final con otro golazo, esta vez producido a partir de una gran recorte y un disparo a la escuadra que tocó en el larguero. Con la flecha para arriba, puso después un centro medido a Boyé que peinó al palo largo para obligar a Radu a hacer una parada salvadora. Los de Quique no dejaron de creer. Mariano también la tuvo de cabeza en el descuento pero, de nuevo Radu, demostró tener unas grandes reflejos para salvar la victoria del Celta.

articles.title: El Clásico de filiales acaba en tablas
articles.standfirst: Duelo de ida y vuelta que acaba en empate (3-3) y con el Real Madrid como colista de la Primera RFEF
articles.summary: Duelo de ida y vuelta que acaba en empate (3-3) y con el Real Madrid como colista de la Primera RFEF
articles.body: Los filiales de Real Madrid y Barcelona empataron (3-3) en el Clásico disputado en Valdebebas. Ambos equipos llegaron a tomar ventaja en el marcador, si bien el punto final deja diferentes sensaciones. El Real Madrid apenas suma dos puntos en cinco jornadas, siendo colista de la Primera RFEF, mientras que el Barcelona está tres puntos y cuatro puestos por encima, aún lejos de la zona alta que ha frecuentado en las últimas temporadas. El Barcelona golpeó a las locales hasta en dos ocasiones en la primera parte. Se adelantó muy pronto, a los siete minutos, y recuperó la ventaja poco después de que Oihane San Martín lograra el empate al cuarto de hora de espectáculo. El Real Madrid logró la remontada en un buen arranque del segundo acto, con dos goles en apenas cuatro minutos que llevaron las firmas de Bea Vélez y Raquel Zuazo. Sin embargo, las azulgrana lograron una nueva igualada a 20 minutos para el final con el que se cerraría el choque. Se trata del quinto Clásico entre filiales disputado hasta la fecha, un pulso que de momento cuenta con dos victorias del Real Madrid, una del Barcelona y dos empates. El último, el firmado este domingo. Ambos conjuntos volverán a enfrentarse el 24 de enero en la Ciudad Deportiva Johan Cruyff.

articles.title: El Nàstic aniquila al Madrileño

articles.summary: Los catalanes superan al filial rojiblanco
articles.body: El Nàstic de Tarragona puso fin a su mala racha con una victoria de prestigio ante el Atlético Madrileño (2-1) en el Nou Estadi Costa Daurada. El conjunto dirigido por Xisco Campos dejó atrás cuatro jornadas consecutivas sin ganar y recuperó la sonrisa ante su afición, en un partido marcado por la lluvia, el frío y la necesidad de volver a sumar los tres puntos Joseda Menargues fue uno de los grandes protagonistas del encuentro al abrir el marcador con un gol espectacular que encarriló el triunfo grana. Posteriormente, Carlos Segura amplió la ventaja y permitió al Nàstic afrontar con mayor tranquilidad el tramo final del partido. El equipo tarraconense supo aprovechar sus oportunidades frente a un filial rojiblanco que quiso llevar la iniciativa y demostrar su calidad ofensiva. Sin embargo, el Atlético Madrileño no se rindió y Koke Mota recortó distancias desde el punto de penalti en el último cuarto de hora, añadiendo emoción a los minutos finales. El Nàstic tuvo que resistir para asegurar una victoria importante tanto por los tres puntos como por la confianza que puede aportar al equipo. Los granas demostraron capacidad para competir ante un rival exigente y rompieron una dinámica negativa que empezaba a pesar. Tras las buenas sensaciones mostradas ante el Real Zaragoza en el choque de la semana pasada, los rojiblancos necesitaban el triunfo para cortar la mala racha de resultados. No pudo ser y se marchan de vacío a Madrid. Al que le sabe a gloria la victoria es un Nàstic que llegaba muy necesitado al choque. articles.title: Alineaciones de Real Madrid y Sevilla para el partido de la jornada 9 de la Liga EA Sports
articles.standfirst: Alta tensión en el Bernabéu en el primer partido con Vinicius sancionado
articles.summary: Alta tensión en el Bernabéu en el primer partido con Vinicius sancionado
articles.body: La tensión alrededor del arbitraje y de los despachos acompaña al Real Madrid en la víspera de una cita que, sobre el papel, invita al optimismo. El Sevilla visita el Santiago Bernabéu en un partido marcado por dos elementos que sobrevuelan el ambiente: la ausencia de Vinicius por sanción y el clima de enfrentamiento que se ha instalado en las últimas semanas entre el club blanco, el colectivo arbitral y Javier Tebas. El equipo de José Mourinho regresa a Chamartín después de una semana en la que el foco ha estado tanto en lo deportivo como fuera del césped. Las declaraciones del técnico portugués, la escalada de tensión con los árbitros y los cruces dialécticos con LaLiga han convertido cada comparecencia en un asunto de máxima atención. En ese escenario aparece un Sevilla que llega a un estadio históricamente poco amable para sus intereses. Porque si hay una estadística que acompaña al conjunto hispalense desde hace años es su enorme dificultad para competir lejos del Sánchez-Pizjuán frente a los tres grandes del fútbol español. Y dentro de esa tendencia, el Bernabéu ocupa un lugar especialmente complicado. Las visitas sevillistas a Chamartín suelen acabar con más sufrimiento que alegrías, en un escenario donde tradicionalmente ha encontrado enormes problemas para sumar. El Madrid, además, afronta el choque con la intención de mantener la fortaleza mostrada en casa y de alargar una dinámica positiva que le permita seguir firme en la pelea por los puestos de cabeza. Lo hará sin Vinicius, una ausencia de peso por la capacidad desequilibrante del brasileño, pero respaldado por un Bernabéu que se presume especialmente caliente después de todo lo ocurrido durante los últimos días. Más allá de los puntos, el partido se presenta como una prueba de carácter. El Madrid busca que el ruido exterior no desvíe su camino. El Sevilla, romper una historia reciente que convierte cada visita a uno de los grandes, y particularmente a Chamartín, en una misión de máxima dificultad. Todo preparado para una noche de alta temperatura en el Bernabéu. Real Madrid: Courtois; Valverde, Konaté, Huijsen, Cucurella; Tchouaméni, Güler, Belligham; Diomande, Endrick y Mbappé. Sevilla: Odysseas; Iglesias, Castrín, Kike Salas, Suazo; Agoumé, Fofana; Vargas, Peque, Félix; Robbie Ure.

articles.title: El Arsenal anestesia al Nottingham Forest y vence con su único tiro a puerta
articles.standfirst: Los de Arteta sacan adelante un partido muy gris y siguen a la estela del Manchester City por el liderato
articles.summary: Los de Arteta sacan adelante un partido muy gris y siguen a la estela del Manchester City por el liderato
articles.body: El Arsenal afrontaba la séptima jornada de la Premier con la necesidad de ganar para seguir la estela de un intratable Manchester City que sigue líder con su pleno histórico. Y pese a afrontar el partido en medio de la exigente doble jornada europea, Arteta volvió a alinear un equipo de absolutas garantías, consciente de la importancia del encuentro en City Ground. Como era de esperar, desde bien pronto el Arsenal se hizo con el control de la pelota, pero con un ritmo tan bajo que no dejó ver el primer disparo hasta el minuto 19. Ndoye aprovechó un error de Calafiori para probar suerte pero su intento fue desviado a córner. El primer acercamiento de los visitantes llegaría pocos minutos después, cómo no, en un saque de esquina, que Gabriel remató de tacón y que taponó su compañero Konsa cuando ya iba para dentro. Havertz inquietó un par de veces más la portería de Sels pero no encontró el camino del gol. La segunda mitad tampoco empezó de una manera radicalmente opuesta, y el Arsenal seguía sufriendo sobre el césped de Nottingham. El primer tiro a puerta del partido llegó en el minuto 54 con el remate de cabeza de Murillo que llegó manso a las manos de Raya. Ni siquiera el triple cambio que introdujo el técnico español a la hora de partido en el que estaba Mikel Merino alteró la velocidad de juego ni las ocasiones del equipo 'gunner', que era incapaz de probar al meta local. Rice amenazó con un tiro arriba en la mejor llegada combinativa del equipo entre Saka, Odegaard y Timber, pero su disparo se fue arriba. Y cuando el partido languidecía y se abocaba al empate sin goles, el Arsenal asestó un golpe mortal con su único tiro a puerta del partido. En el minuto 80, Madueke encaró hacia dentro desde la izquierda y su disparo tocó en un defensor para desviar ligeramente y despistar al portero belga. Parecía que el Arsenal conseguía dormir el partido, pero Murillo se vistió de Ronaldo Nazario para llevar el miedo al cuerpo de los aficionados 'gunners' con una jugada tremenda. Konsa taponó de manera milagrosa el último disparo de Delap, y el equipo de Mikel Arteta vuelve a sacar adelante un partido trabado e importante de los que se puede acordar uno a final de temporada para seguir a tres puntos y a la caza de un City que sigue imparable en estos primeros siete partidos.

articles.title: Revolución en el Bernabéu: la hora de la meritocracia de Mourinho
articles.standfirst: El entrenador portugués estrena dos tridentes y lanza un aviso a los laterales derechos
articles.summary: El entrenador portugués estrena dos tridentes y lanza un aviso a los laterales derechos
articles.body: José Mourinho ha decidido romper el tablero a una semana del Clásico en el Camp Nou. La visita del Sevilla al Bernabéu no admitía medias tintas, y el técnico portugués ha respondido con una auténtica declaración de intenciones: una revolución total en el once titular que premia el rendimiento visto en Roma por encima de los galones. La gran atracción de la noche será, sin duda, la primera titularidad de Endrick. El delantero brasileño derribó la puerta de la titularidad tras su exhibición en Champions, donde su entrada al campo revolucionó un partido que parecía perdido. Sin el sancionado Vinicius en los planes, Mourinho apuesta por el descaro y la potencia del carioca para dinamitar la banda derecha y aportar esa pegada contundente que el madridismo tanto le exige a un equipo obligado a ganar, convencer... y dominar el partido. El giro estratégico más ambicioso se vivirá en la sala de máquinas, donde se estrena un centro del campo completamente renovado y enfocado a la creatividad. En busca de posesión, fluidez del balón, combinando el músculo y el equilibrio de hombres como Tchouaméni con la magia entre líneas de Arda Güler y Jude Bellingham. El plan de Mourinho es tan agresivo como claro: asfixiar al rival en su propio campo y generar juego ofensivo desde el primer minuto. Por último, otra de las sorpresas del once es el primer partido de Valverde arrancando en el lateral derecho. Con Trent y Dumfries en el banquillo, el uruguayo vivirá su primera noche en banda.

articles.title: Mario Gila se estrena como goleador en el triunfo del Milan
articles.standfirst: El defensa español completó el momentáneo 3-0 para los locales
articles.summary: El defensa español completó el momentáneo 3-0 para los locales
articles.body: El Milan se impuso por 3-2 al Atalanta en un partido que parecía tener encarrilado, con tres goles de ventaja, pero en el que acabó sufriendo tras la reacción del conjunto de Maurizio Sarri en la segunda mitad. El encuentro enfrentó a dos equipos que llegaron con la intención de consolidar sus últimas buenas sensaciones, aunque con distintos objetivos inmediatos. El Milan buscó recuperarse en la Serie A tras su tropiezo ante el Sassuolo, mientras que el Atalanta aspiró a prolongar el impulso de su victoria europea frente al Pafos. El conjunto milanista llevó la iniciativa desde el pitido inicial, con mayor posesión y capacidad para instalarse en campo contrario del equipo de Maurizio Sarri. También con el mayor número de oportunidades para abrir el marcador. La acción resultó especialmente costosa para los visitantes, que poco después perdieron por lesión al central Sead Kolasinac. Su sustituto, el joven Relja Obric, acabó siendo protagonista del primer gol milanista. En el minuto 23, tocó con la mano un disparo de Yunus Musah dentro del área y el árbitro, tras revisar la jugada en el VAR, señaló penalti. Goncalo Ramos transformó la pena máxima. Fue un tanto fundamental para devolver la confianza al delantero, el fichaje más caro de la historia milanista, que no logró demostrar todavía con el Milan su sed goleadora como sí que hizo durante el parón de selecciones con Portugal. Aunque se fue con sabor agridulce al fallar un segundo penalti minutos después. El Milan aprovechó el golpe para afianzar su dominio. Diego Moreira, muy activo por la banda izquierda, encontró a Rabiot con un pase filtrado en el minuto 43. El francés se acomodó el balón, superó a Obric y batió a Marco Carnesecchi con un disparo raso al primer palo para establecer el 2-0 antes del descanso. Tras la reanudación, el equipo de Amorim mantuvo el control del juego. En el minuto 56, el conjunto local dispuso de un segundo penalti por una mano de Joakim Kristensen en un disparo de Rabiot. Esta vez, sin embargo, Carnesecchi adivinó el lanzamiento de Ramos y evitó el tercer tanto. Un minuto después, el español Mario Gila puso el 3-0. Su primero como milanista. El Atalanta encontró una respuesta en el minuto 66. Nicola Zalewski, recién ingresado al campo, puso un balón desde la izquierda para Gianluca Gaetano, que controló dentro del área y conectó un potente disparo con la zurda que superó a Maignan. El conjunto de Sarri adelantó líneas y encontró premio en el 81, cuando Raoul Bellanova desbordó por la derecha y puso un pase raso que Nikola Krstovic convirtió en el 3-2. El tanto cambió el escenario de un partido que el Milan dominó durante buena parte del duelo. El empate estuvo cerca en el minuto 84, cuando Davide Zappacosta aprovechó un error defensivo de De Winter para plantarse ante Mike Maignan. El guardameta francés respondió con una gran parada y evitó que el Atalanta culminara su reacción. El Milan se endosó al final los tres puntos, no sin antes sufrir.

articles.title: Aston Villa’s £30m Warning Sign: Can Emery Replace Lost Experience Under PSR?
articles.summary: St James’ Park doesn’t hand out points. Villa left it on Saturday with a 1-0 win, and the man who settled it was Johan Manzambi, a 21-year-old Swiss internat...
articles.body:
St James' Park doesn't hand out points. Villa left it on Saturday with a 1-0 win, and the man who settled it was Johan Manzambi, a 21-year-old Swiss international who snubbed Newcastle in July to sign for Villa Park. Unai Emery, never one for gloating, will have counted the three points and glanced at the table.

Emery's squad looks different now. Villa sold Morgan Rogers to Chelsea for £120m and watched Ollie Watkins leave too, part of roughly £500m in sales across several years to keep the books inside Premier League profit rules and UEFA's squad cost limits. One summer wiped 489 Premier League appearances out of the dressing room.

Football Insider has now put a price on the damage. Stefan Borson, a former Manchester City financial adviser, told the outlet that Villa's league form could cancel out their Champions League riches. Emery's side sit third in the European table after two games and are closing on a £12.1m windfall, but the Premier League tells another story. When the report appeared, Villa were 16th, two points clear of the relegation zone.

Borson values each league place at roughly £3m in prize money. Fourth last season means a deep slide could cost up to £30m, and a seven-place drop alone takes away £21m. He reckons the turnaround is harder after so many summer changes. Opta's supercomputer is kinder, tipping eighth place and 51 points, yet even that is four places lower than last season and a £12m shortfall.

Villa paid Freiburg £51m for Manzambi, a club record. Money like that demands output. His best weapon is the carry: pick the ball up deep, drive at a back line, drag three defenders out of shape. Balance is excellent, pressing barely bothers him, and he arrives in the box late.

Weaknesses exist. His defensive positioning can drift, the final pass sometimes lacks cleanness, and a 21-year-old's body has to survive a Premier League winter. Emery loves midfielders who push the ball forward quickly and press in packs, so Manzambi suits the plan. Nicolas Jackson's arrival adds clinical effectiveness up front.

Can Emery balance lost experience with PSR demands, and does Manzambi justify the pivot?

BIRMINGHAM, ENGLAND – OCTOBER 13: Unai Emery, Manager of Aston Villa, speaks to the media during the press conference on day ahead of the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 at Bodymoor Heath training ground on October 13, 2026 in Birmingham, England. (Photo by Morgan Harlow/Getty Images)

Emery can balance it only by trusting shape over names. Villa lost leaders, but the structure he drills every day survives changes in personnel better than most. Experienced replacements cost money the club doesn't have, so he leans on routines: a compact press, quick vertical passes, set-piece patterns rehearsed to the point of boredom. Youth carries risk away from home, and Newcastle showed it carries reward too.

Manzambi justifies the pivot on this evidence. £51m is a heavy label for a 21-year-old, and the winner at St James' Park came from exactly the sort of player Villa could never have afforded at 28. Resale value matters under profit rules. A young international with rising numbers protects the books rather than straining them.

Borson's £30m warning is real money, and the cure is simple: points. Every place climbed returns roughly £3m. Emery needs the league table to catch up with the European one, and Jackson's finishing plus Manzambi's carrying hand him the tools. Experience will return slowly, through Manzambi's second and third seasons and through a willingness to keep the young core together rather than cash out at the first big bid.

articles.title: World Cup winner turned down move to Liverpool
articles.summary: Nico Williams Agent Reveals Why Liverpool Missed Out on Athletic Club StarLiverpool’s interest in Nico Williams during the summer of 2024 was well documented...
articles.body:
Nico Williams Agent Reveals Why Liverpool Missed Out on Athletic Club Star

Liverpool's interest in Nico Williams during the summer of 2024 was well documented, but fresh comments from the Spanish winger's agent have provided a fascinating insight into why a move to Anfield never materialised.

The Athletic Club forward was one of European football's most sought-after players following his outstanding performances at Euro 2024. Liverpool were among several elite clubs pursuing his signature, although convincing Williams to leave Bilbao proved considerably more complicated than anticipated.

Liverpool Faced Fierce Competition for Nico Williams

Williams entered the summer of 2024 with his reputation soaring. Having helped Athletic Club secure the Copa del Rey, he went on to play a decisive role in Spain's European Championship triumph, scoring against England in the final.

His explosive pace, direct running and ability to operate across the attacking positions made him an attractive proposition for Liverpool, who were preparing for their first season under Arne Slot.

However, Liverpool faced competition from Barcelona, Arsenal, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain.

Speaking to Spanish outlet Los Fulanos , Williams' agent Felix Tainta has now revealed the extraordinary level of interest in his client.

"Barcelona, Arsenal, Bayern, Liverpool, Paris Saint-Germain… I could name them all. Everyone wanted Nico, and having a player say no to all these clubs isn't easy," he said.

That admission raises an interesting question about how much influence a player's personal circumstances can have on even the most ambitious transfer negotiations.

Playing Time Proved Crucial to Williams Decision

According to Tainta, guarantees over playing opportunities were central to Williams' thinking.

"We decided that if there weren't certain guarantees, we couldn't risk Nico not going there to play, with a World Cup coming up, and not just with a World Cup. A professional has to practice their profession," he added.

There is considerable logic behind that position.

For a young international approaching his prime, consistent football offers an opportunity to develop, maintain momentum and strengthen his position within the national team.

Liverpool already possessed significant attacking quality in 2024, meaning Williams would have faced considerable competition for minutes.

Whether Liverpool were unwilling to provide specific assurances remains unclear. Tainta's comments describe the broader decision-making process without identifying precisely what each interested club offered.

That distinction matters when assessing Liverpool's recruitment strategy.

Athletic Club Commitment Reflects Williams Priorities

Williams ultimately remained with Athletic Club, strengthening his connection with a club where he had developed into one of Spain's most exciting attacking talents.

His subsequent decision to sign a remarkable ten-year contract extension, keeping him at Bilbao until 2035, demonstrated the strength of that commitment.

For Athletic Club, retaining a player coveted by Europe's wealthiest clubs represented a significant achievement.

For Liverpool, the episode illustrates the challenges involved in recruiting established international talents who already enjoy considerable status and security at their existing clubs.

The financial package, sporting project and prospect of silverware all matter, but so does the player's assessment of his immediate career prospects.

Liverpool Transfer Lesson Remains Relevant Under Iraola

With Andoni Iraola now overseeing Liverpool's next chapter, Williams' situation offers a useful reminder about recruitment.

Elite attacking players naturally attract interest from multiple clubs, and negotiations frequently depend on factors beyond transfer fees and wages.

Williams clearly valued regular football and his established position at Athletic Club.

Liverpool's interest was genuine enough to feature among the clubs named by his representative, but the winger ultimately chose continuity.

Given his long-term contract, any future Liverpool pursuit would present substantial complications.

For now, Tainta's revelations provide a clearer understanding of why one of European football's most coveted wingers remained in Bilbao despite Liverpool's interest.

articles.summary: Un golazo de Bryan Gil y un error clamoroso de Owono cortan la buena racha de resultados del equipo del Principado
articles.body: El Girona sumó tres puntos vitales para mantenerse en los primeros vagones del tren de equipos que lucharán por el ascenso después de superar un Andorra voluntarioso, pero sin suficiente veneno en ataque. Dos goles de Bryan Gil y Vanat, de soberbia falta directa el primero y tras un error clamoroso de Owono el segundo, permiten al Girona reencontrarse con la victoria dos empates después, regresando así a zona de 'playoffs', mientras los del Principado, pese a tener la posesión e instalarse en campo rival la segunda parte, no pudieron meterse en el partido, vuelven a perder tras tres jornadas sumando y se quedan marcando la zona de permanencia. El inicio del partido no pudo ser mejor para el Girona, que después de unos instantes, pocos, de tanteo aprovechó una falta a unos cinco metros de la frontal para avanzarse en el marcador. Bryan Gil asumió la responsabilidad y con un potente disparo sorprendió a Owono, que después de hacer un paso a su izquierda no llegó a tiempo a estirarse a la derecha para defender su palo. El gol le sentó de maravilla a un equipo blanquirrojo que pese a no tener la posesión presionó y robo en campo contrario, algo que le ayudó a estar cerca de la portería rival en más ocasiones que el rival aunque sin inquietar en exceso. Y es que, el 2-0 llegó sin tener que formular ni una jugada ofensiva ya que Owono, en el intento arriesgadísimo de regatear a Vanat, regaló el gol al ucraniano, que puso el pie y le robó el esférico para marcar a placer. Un duro golpe para un Andorra que solo tuvo una ocasión en el añadido del primer acto, cuando Francés se pasó de frenada y Jordi Cano, al que antes habían anulado un gol por claro fuera de juego, pudo rematar ante un Gazzaniga que envió a córner con el pie. En la segunda parte, pese al triple cambio de inicio de la escuadra tricolor, la tónica no cambio para nada. El Andorra controló la posesión y se instaló en campo catalán con más regularidad para crear alguna ocasión más, aunque demasiado tímidas. Las más claras las tuvieron Moro Sidibe con un remate de cabeza muy centrado y Efe Akman, con un lanzamiento desde cerca de la frontal con rosca que Gazzaniga envió a saque de esquina. Los de Quique Álvarez intentaron estirar líneas y Asprilla, nada más saltar al campo, pudo hacer la sentencia si no hubiera cruzado demasiado un remate con el interior de su zurda que salió rozando el poste.

articles.title: Why some Real Madrid board members are already turning on José Mourinho
articles.summary: Sections of the boardroom at La Liga giants Real Madrid are already growing frustrated with the efforts of José Mourinho across the season to date. This come...
articles.body:
Sections of the boardroom at La Liga giants Real Madrid are already growing frustrated with the efforts of José Mourinho across the season to date. This comes for a whole host of reasons, on and off the pitch alike.

Real Madrid have of course endured something of a hit-and-miss campaign all told to date. Across 10 fixtures in all competitions, Los Blancos have emerged triumphant all but twice.

Their performances along the way, however, have too often left a lot to be desired, lacking cohesion and a consistent pattern of play.

Not only that, but the relentless nature of Hansi Flick's Barcelona means that defeat in next weekend's El Clásico could all but end Real's La Liga title chances by October.

And as alluded to above, amongst some sections of the boardroom at the Bernabéu, the finger of blame is being pointed in the direction of José Mourinho…

As per a report from club insider Jorge C Picon:

'There are doubts from the executive suites. There are important voices in the club that aren't convinced by what they're seeing. The scant presence of Diomande in the starting lineups and some change with Arda Güler that they considered untimely didn't sit well either.

'They expected the margin of decision to translate into a more visible overhaul. However, there are too many similarities with last season, in the style of play and in some decisions. The excitement that accompanied his return has given way, in part of the club, to a more demanding gaze.'

articles.title: Arteta delighted for ‘decisive’ Madueke in win over Nottingham Forest
articles.summary: Mikel Arteta hailed Noni Madueke as a “special guy” after the winger scored the winner in Arsenal’s 1-0 victory over Nottingham Forest.Madueke struck the dec...
articles.body:
Mikel Arteta hailed Noni Madueke as a "special guy" after the winger scored the winner in Arsenal's 1-0 victory over Nottingham Forest.

Madueke struck the decisive goal at the City Ground and Arteta believes the England international is beginning to show another level to his game.

"Noni, look at me, a smile on my face because he's a special character," Arteta said.

"He's someone very much loved in and around the dressing room, the way he talks to people, he's just a special guy.

"I think I saw an interview with our players where they were asking, who would you call if you had a problem? And some of them said Noni, which I was surprised about but I think it's massive credit and explains the kind of person that he is."

Arteta also praised Madueke's growing influence on matches.

"I think after the break, he's showing something else, another level of anger and conviction as well in his actions and is becoming decisive in matches which is what we expect from a player like him."

Arsenal were made to work hard for the victory, with Forest sitting deep and frustrating Arteta's side for long periods.

"There have been other games where we've scored in the first half," Arteta said.

"We've played 11 competitive matches and won ten. There are a variety of ways to win.

"They are extremely well organised, they put like a Christmas tree there and there is no space to play.

"You have to be so neat and tidy or otherwise generate a lot of chaos in the box whether in open play or set-pieces."

Arteta felt patience was key as Arsenal waited for spaces to open up later in the game.

"The longer game goes, we have to play a different game," he said.

"Because the moment we start to ramp up our level of frustration, the game is going to be really dangerous for us because we're going to take more risk, as we should, but the players occupying certain spaces to control the transitions are going to be instrumental.

"I had the belief that the moment the physical level dropped, the spaces would be a little bit bigger, the timing more, and we'll be more efficient there, and the finishers delivered because the game changed."

The victory made it ten wins from Arsenal's first 11 competitive matches, and Arteta believes his side are in a strong position despite still having room to improve.

"11 games, ten wins, after inheriting 18 players coming from the World Cup," he said.

"I think we're in a good place, we can always improve and we should improve and that's the ambition.

"It shows how difficult it is. To expect another kind of game, it's not the reality of the league.

"We win in this way and almost every team is winning in that manner. I think the level has gone up again and we'll have more and more surprises."

articles.title: First Bundesliga loss for Freiburg, Monaco no longer unbeaten in France and Madrid without Vinícius
articles.summary: MADRID (AP) — Freiburg wasted a chance to regain first place in the Bundesliga with its first loss of the season on Sunday — a 2-1 defeat at Bayer Leverkusen...
articles.body:
MADRID (AP) — Freiburg wasted a chance to regain first place in the Bundesliga with its first loss of the season on Sunday — a 2-1 defeat at Bayer Leverkusen — and Monaco lost 1-0 at Lorient to lose its status of the only unbeaten team in the French league.

Diego Gomez scored off a shot from the halfway line in Brighton's 5-0 win over Crystal Palace, and Arsenal edged Nottingham Forest in the Premier League .

Real Madrid will be without Vinícius Júnior for its home game against Sevilla later Sunday in La Liga .

Freiburg took the lead through Derry Scherhant in the 14th minute but the hosts rallied with goals from Ibrahim Maza in the 19th and Patrik Schick in the 76th.

Freiburg stayed with 13 points, one point behind both second-place Borussia Dortmund and leader Bayern Munich.

Only Frankfurt had managed to take points off Freiburg, which had won eight of its last nine games across all competitions.

The club has consistently overachieved in recent seasons despite modest resources, first under coach Christian Streich, now under his former captain Julian Schuster, who took over from the veteran in 2024.

Schuster led the team to the Europa League final last season, which it lost to Aston Villa.

Leverkusen has also made a good start under new coach Carles Martínez, who has now overseen six wins from seven games across all competitions since starting with a shock loss to Elversberg.

Last-place Borussia Mönchengladbach lost 2-1 to visiting Hoffenheim, which had lost every match since a 2-1 win over Stuttgart a month ago.

Gomez's sensational strike came after the Paraguay international collected the ball near the halfway line, advanced just inside Palace's half and launched a 50-meter shot over stranded goalkeeper Walter Benitez in the seventh minute.

Arsenal, the Premier League defending champion, just needed one goal — a late one from substitute Noni Madueke — to see off Nottingham Forest 1-0.

Manchester United ended a challenging week with a 1-1 draw at fierce rival Leeds.

Monaco was guaranteed to retain first place with a win, but host Lorient won thanks to a 61st-minute penalty kick converted by Noah Cadiou.

Lorient moved to seventh place, while Monaco dropped to fourth and is tied on 14 points with leader Paris Saint-Germain, second-place Paris FC and Lille. Paris needed a penalty kick deep into stoppage time to defeat fifth-place Rennes 4-3 at home.

Marseille's form has been bleak this season and new coach Bruno Genesio's side had won only two of its first eight games overall, but it came from behind to win 5-2 at Angers.

Celta Vigo beat Alaves 2-1 at home for its second win across all competitions this season. The result left Celta in eighth place, level on 11 points with seventh-place Alaves, which won three of its first four league games but is winless in five straight.

Osasuna defeated Racing Santander 2-0 as Jagoba Arrasate coached his first game since returning to Osasuna. He replaced the fired Luis Ramis after a run of five winless games. Arrasate has coached the second-most games in the history of the Pamplona-based club.

Madrid's Vinícius will serve the first of a four-game suspension later Sunday for pulling the hair of a Villarreal player and aggressively confronting the referee in the previous round.

In Italy, Como won 3-1 at second-to-last Fiorentina, while 11th-place Lecce won 3-0 at 17th-place Udinese.

AC Milan hosted Atalanta later Sunday while coming off a morale-boosting 4-0 win over Salzburg in the Europa League.

Milan is one of four teams undefeated in Serie A, along with rival Inter Milan, Lazio and Roma.

Lazio faced Juventus, whose coach Luciano Spalletti is serving a one-match suspension following his altercation with Cagliari coach Fabio Pisacane.

articles.title: Snaps and analysis from Broncos win over Seahawks on TNF
articles.summary: The Denver Broncos inactives on Thursday Night Football against the Seattle Seahawks were QB Sam Ehlinger, DL Jordan Jackson, CB Pat Surtain II, S Talanoa Hu...
articles.body:
The Denver Broncos inactives on Thursday Night Football against the Seattle Seahawks were QB Sam Ehlinger, DL Jordan Jackson, CB Pat Surtain II, S Talanoa Hufanga, TE Dallen Bentley, OL Kage Casey, and DL Tyler Onyedim.

The five starting offensive linemen and Bo Nix played all 60 offensive snaps. Alex Palczewski played one snap as the 6th offensive lineman.

JK Dobbins, RJ Harvey, Tyler Badie and Adam Prentice played 31, 24, 5, and 4 snaps. Dobbins had 20 touches on his 31 snaps. Harvey had 9 on his 24 snaps. Dobbins getting the ball 65 percent of the time he was in the game, seems like it would be a big tell for the opposing defense. Dobbins 20 touches resulted in 46 yards of total offense (17 runs, 3 catches). That's 2.3 yards per touch, which is pathetic. For comparison, Harvey's nine touches resulted in 56 yards, 6.2 yards per touch, which is almost triple what Dobbins got. Dobbins may have hit the age-wall that eventually gets all running backs. He doesn't appear to have any burst this year.

Even Engram, Adam Trautman, and Nate Adkins played 31, 33, and 22 snaps. Only Engram was targetted getting two catches for 13 yards on his two targets.

Courtland Sutton, Jaylen Waddle, Troy Franklin, Lil'Jordan Humphrey, and Marvin Mims played 46, 41, 39, 17 and 16 snaps on offense. They combined for 15 targets and 9 catches, but the longest of those went for only 10 yards. The Broncos had three plays on the day that gained 10 or more yards, 16 x 2, and 10 x 1.

The only active offensive player who did not get in the game was Jarrett Stidham.

Three defenders played all 85 snaps, Jahdae Barron, Alex Singleton, and Brandon Jones.

Taylor Rapp played 76% of the defensive snaps at the other safety spot. Devon Key got 34% of the defensive snaps, so the Broncos ran three safeties for eight or nine snaps during the game.

At CB, Riley Moss was only able to play 20 snaps, while Kris Abrams-Draine and Ja'Quan McMillian both played 65 snaps.

Justin Strnad played played 76 snaps at the other ILB spot. We only used two ILBs on defense.

At OLB Nik Bonitto, Jonah Elliss, Que Robinson, and Dondrea Tillman played 48, 38, 43, and 41 snaps. This was big jump for Tillman and Robinson. In the previous six games, Bonitto and Elliss had been getting the majority of the snaps with Robinson and Tillman getting about half as many. Using all four equally (roughly) was a new wrinkle for Vance Joseph. I wonder who will be losing snaps next game when Jonathan Cooper returns.

Zah Allen, Eyioma Uwazurike, Malcolm Roach, DJ and Sai'vion Jones, played 57, 45, 42, 24, and 22 snaps.

The Broncos had six player who were in on 74 percent or more of the special team snaps. Que Robinson, Dondrea Tillman, Devon Key, JL Skinner, and Tycen Anderson.

articles.title: La Real se ensaña con un débil Málaga
articles.standfirst: El conjunto txuriurdin se impuso por 2-5 en La Rosaleda, al superar al conjunto local y aprovechar mucho mejor sus ocasiones, sobre todo en la segunda parte
articles.summary: El conjunto txuriurdin se impuso por 2-5 en La Rosaleda, al superar al conjunto local y aprovechar mucho mejor sus ocasiones, sobre todo en la segunda parte
articles.body: La Real Sociedad se reencontró ayer con LaLiga tras su disgusto europeo del jueves de la mejor manera posible, ya que sumó su cuarta victoria en las últimas cinco jornadas y en esta ocasión con goleada, ya que se ensañó con un Málaga débil y con mala suerte y le metió un 2-5, con Kubo y Oyarzabal estrenándose este curso como goleadores. El partido no pudo comenzar mejor para la Real, ya que en su primer ataque, Take Kubo tuvo la fortuna de que su chut tocó leve pero lo suficiente en la bota de Pablo Martínez como para coger una parábola espectacular y colarse por la misma escuadra derecha de la portería de Herrero, cuando no habían pasado ni tres minutos. El Málaga no se vino abajo e intentó competir en posesión de balón y en ocasiones, pero Remiro se sacó una mano espectacular ante un remate a bocajarro de Adrián Niño para evitar el empate. El de Cascante, no contento con ello, estuvo cerca de ser asistente de Óskarsson, pero el chut cruzado del islandés se fue por poco. El 9 de Matarazzo se desquitó enseguida, porque a los dos minutos aprovechó un balón que le llegó de rebote para esta vez sí batir por bajo al meta local y poner el 0-2. Barrenetxea tuvo el tercero en la siguiente acción, pero no atinó. Los locales lo volvieron a intentar, pero a Chupe se le fue alto el derechazo. Oyarzabal y Jon Martín sí mandaron la pelota a portería, pero Herrero despejó la del campeón del mundo y un defensa la del central, antes del descanso. La Real, a través de la cabeza de Sarr, fue la primera en crear peligro tras el paso por los vestuarios, pero el balón se fue fuera, deteniendo luego Herrero el disparo de Soler. El Málaga, con Funes dando entrada a Ramón y Aznou para la segunda parte, reaccionó otra vez y ahora con premio, al poner el 1-2 Adrián Niño con un derechazo cercano imposible para Remiro. La esperanza le duró muy poco al conjunto malagueño, porque Oyarzabal se reencontró con el gol, con un potente zurdazo ajustado al palo corto de Herrero. Como suele ser habitual en los encuentros de los de Matarazzo, el partido se volvió loco, con un cabezazo al travesaño de Chupe y de inmediato el 2-3 con un espectacular voleón de Pablo Martínez. La Real no dejó esta vez que hubiese mucha emoción, porque un minuto después Oyarzabal se soltó otro zurdazo similar al anterior para firmar el doblete y poner el 2-4, con Guedes haciendo el quinto, tras remate al larguero de Óskarsson. El luso rozó el sexto, pero la pelota salió rozando el palo, con un susto de Oyarzabal afortunadamente sin consecuencias antes del pitido final.
